producer_report.summary: Built the Hestia sweep skeleton, the findings record, and the `athena hestia sweep` and `athena hestia last` commands. D129 is now accepted. A new record, `athena.hestia-sweep/1`, is stored at `records/hestia-sweeps/<YYYY-MM>/<id>.json`. It lists every check with how many things it examined and how many findings it reported, plus the findings. A check that returns an error does not stop the sweep: `run_sweep` turns the error into an open finding for that check and marks the check as errored, so it never looks clean. A finding with no subject or no evidence is handled the same way. No checks ship yet: `default_checks()` is empty. A sweep with no checks is still recorded and prints "no checks registered". `last` prints "no sweep recorded; run `athena hestia sweep` to make one" when nothing exists. The trigger is settled as an explicit command. D129 records the alternatives: a drain hook is deferred, and a timer or daemon is rejected for now. `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with warnings denied are clean. The full `cargo test --locked` returned without a failure exit code, but I could not read its output, so I did not confirm the counts.

checks_run.note: 2 record tests: round trip with path and schema, and rejection of mismatched counts, duplicate ids, stray checks and empty evidence. The `latest` test is named `the_latest_sweep_...`, so this filter skips it; it runs under plain `cargo test -p athena-data`.
5 tests: clean checks, error becoming a finding, finding without evidence, empty default checks, and a committed sweep read back with the newest returned.
3 renderer tests: none recorded, a sweep with an errored check and a finding, and a clean or empty sweep.
Printed the no-sweep message in the work repository. I did not run `hestia sweep` there, to avoid committing a record into the work tree.
The command returned without a failure exit code. The output was too large to display and I could not open the saved copy, so I did not read the per-suite counts.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs registers several checks that each return no findings. The resulting report lists every check by id with a count of 0 and has no findings. Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`. Test `a_sweep_where_every_check_finds_nothing_lists_every_check_with_a_count_of_zero` passes. It checks three checks (alpha, beta, gamma) with count 0, examined 3, 0 and 12, not errored, and an empty findings list.

criteria_check.criterion: A unit test has one check return an error while the others succeed. The report holds a finding for that check (check id, subject, evidence containing the error, age, state), and the other checks are still listed with counts. Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`. Test `a_check_that_errors_becomes_a_finding_and_the_other_checks_still_run` passes. For the broken check it asserts count 1, errored, subject equal to the check id, evidence containing "cannot read the branch list", age 0 and state open. The other checks are still listed with their counts.

criteria_check.criterion: A record-level test shows a swept report round-trips through athena-data records.rs and that reading the last sweep returns the most recent one. Run `cargo test -p athena-data`.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-data hestia`: round trip, path, schema and validation tests pass. The test `the_latest_sweep_is_the_most_recent_by_time_whatever_the_order` covers `HestiaSweep::latest` and runs under plain `cargo test -p athena-data`. I did not run it separately by name. Core test `a_committed_sweep_is_read_back_and_the_last_one_is_the_newest` also passes in athena-core.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo run -- hestia last` (or the equivalent athena-cli invocation) prints the last sweep, listing each check with its count and each finding. With no sweep recorded it prints an explicit 'no sweep recorded' message, not an empty success. A CLI test covers both cases.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo run -q --bin athena -- hestia last`; it printed "no sweep recorded; run `athena hestia sweep` to make one". The workspace has two binaries, so plain `cargo run -- hestia last` needs `--bin athena`. `cargo test -p athena-cli hestia` passes. The tests in crates/athena-cli/src/lib.rs cover the no-sweep message and a sweep with per-check counts, an errored marker, and a finding with check, subject, age, state and evidence. They test the renderer, not a spawned binary; main.rs only calls `last_sweep` and the renderer. I did not run `hestia sweep` through the binary.

criteria_check.criterion: Finding has the fields check id, subject, evidence, age and state, as specified in docs/design/hestia.md §9 job 1, and the module is exported from crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: `HestiaFinding` in athena-data/src/records.rs has `check`, `subject`, `evidence`, `age_seconds` and `state`. `athena_core::hestia::Finding` re-exports it, and lib.rs has `pub mod hestia;`. Tests build the type with all five fields.

open_issues: I changed files outside the brief's deliverable list. crates/athena-core/src/store.rs is needed: Records::load matches AnyRecord exhaustively, and an unlisted variant would hit its panic arm, so I added `hestia_sweeps` there and to `has_record_id`. docs/records.md (record directory listing) and docs/design/roadmap.md ("proposed in D129" changed to "accepted") are small doc fixes.
Finding age is stored as whole seconds (`age_seconds`, 0 for new).
A sweep with no registered checks still commits a record. A later job may decide that is noise.
The CLI test covers the renderer, not a spawned `athena hestia last` process. The wiring was shown by running the binary once, not by a test.
The brief's `cargo run -- hestia last` does not work as written because the workspace has two binaries; use `cargo run --bin athena -- hestia last`.
mistakes: My first command piped to `tail`, which the policy denied. I reran it without the pipe.
I ran plain `cargo run -- hestia last` before knowing the workspace has two binaries; it failed until I added `--bin athena`.
I could not open the saved full-suite output to confirm per-suite results, so the full test result rests on the absence of a failure exit code.
learnings: The workspace has two binaries (athena, xtask), so `cargo run` needs `--bin athena`.

Records::load matches AnyRecord exhaustively, and a new variant that is not listed there reaches the "every other record names its job" panic arm. A new record type must be added to the load, the path, the schema and `has_record_id`.
A core test can commit records with a plain git repository that holds athena.toml and defaults.toml, built the way the invocation tests do, with no cutover fixture.
`cargo fmt` rewrites files in the working tree, so files must be re-read before further edits.
The producer policy blocks Bash pipes and `tail`, and the Grep tool cannot read a saved tool-result file outside the working directory.
desires: A way to read a persisted large tool-output file, or a test summary mode, so a full-suite pass can be confirmed from the output rather than the exit code.
